A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoTree. All 23 pages of v2 and 19 pages of v3, including appendices and supplementary material, support comparison. Equations, algorithms, tables and figures can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original VideoTree benchmark accuracies, efficiency measurements, ablations and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds benchmark evaluations, ablations and a human assessment of keyframe relevance scoring.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same clustering, adaptive breadth expansion, relevance-guided depth expansion and temporally ordered caption reasoning. Short-clip captioning and retention of parent-cluster information are clarified. Alternative captioning and ordering procedures are evaluated as ablations without replacing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 retains EgoSchema, NExT-QA, IntentQA and Video-MME long evaluations. Section 8.2 adds MLVU validation and Video-MME short/medium evaluations, extending the represented video data and duration coverage within the existing video-understanding focus.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LLoVi and Oryx-1.5-34B to the Video-MME long comparison. Table 6 adds LLaVA-OV-72B and LongVU to the EgoSchema comparison. Existing comparators remain; the Tarsier-34B and InternVL2-34B labels identify previously reported comparators more precisely.

E3.justification: New evaluations specify LLaVA-OV-7B captioning, alternative encoder/prompt/ordering controls, and comparison with one annotator over 345 keyframes from 20 EgoSchema videos. Figure 3 adds LLoVi conditions at 45 and 90 captions and VideoAgent at approximately 14 captions. Existing main evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond retained ablations and qualitative cases, v3 adds DINOv2 encoder testing, question-prompted captioning, tree-traversal versus temporal caption ordering, and human validation of relevance scores (Sections 9 and 12). These substantially extend tests of component choices and the hierarchy's role. Figure 3 also expands the caption-budget sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added human-agreement percentage is a new evaluation result, not uncertainty estimation. The prompts' self-reported confidence requests are retained.

E6.justification: Headline accuracies remain 61.1% on EgoSchema, 75.6% on NExT-QA and 54.2% on Video-MME long. Substantial additional results include Table 8's 67.8%/59.9% on Video-MME short/medium and 60.4% on MLVU; DINOv2 at 64.2%; question-prompted captioning at 63.2%; tree ordering at 64.8% versus temporal ordering at 66.2%; and 90.7% human agreement. Tables 2/6 and Figure 3 add comparator results, including LLoVi's 61.8% at 90 captions.

T1.justification: The clustering definition in Equation 1 and the algorithmic formulation remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3 adds no substantive mathematical assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contribution: training-free, query-adaptive hierarchical video selection that improves reasoning accuracy and efficiency. The abstract's headline results are unchanged. The conclusion's outlook on stronger modular components was already discussed in v2 Appendix A.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes the tree's value for frame selection from temporal ordering's value for reasoning, and interprets the human-agreement results. It removes v2's explicit QA-stage hallucination and proprietary-model update/retirement caveats while retaining captioner limitations and the failure case. Table 1 adds an overbroad superiority statement despite LVNet's 68.2% versus VideoTree's 66.2% on the EgoSchema subset.

D1.justification: Section 11 newly specifies initial cluster counts: 4 for NExT-QA and 8 for EgoSchema and Video-MME. Existing hyperparameters, prompts and hardware details remain. v3 removes the statement that code accompanies the supplementary material and the license/access listing, while retaining the project homepage. This establishes a documentation change, not an actual change in external code availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 explicitly credits coarse-to-fine predecessors as inspiration and adds LiteEval. New references include LLaVA-OneVision, Oryx, DINOv2 and LongVU; CREMA and the hallucination-survey reference disappear. The main positioning around structured video representations and LLM reasoning remains.

P1.justification: The prose receives localized rewrites and methodological clarifications, shorter section headings and a revised conclusion. The visual-encoder analysis moves to the supplement, lettered appendices become Sections 7–12, and standalone ethics, reproducibility and licensing sections disappear. Most narrative content and its sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. The original Table 5 is split between main text and supplement, Table 4 is reorganized, and Table 8 is added. Figure 3 is redrawn and extended; the other five figures are retained. The threshold table's incorrect Max Breadth heading is corrected.

improvement.justification: The additional benchmark evaluations, ordering control and human relevance check provide useful validation absent from v2, while disclosure of initial cluster counts improves reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removed code/license documentation and reporting problems: Table 1 overstates superiority, and the new captioner comparison calls 63.2% three points worse despite Table 14 reporting 59.2% for the unconditioned LLaVA captioner.
